teardown.hook: Why did Apple lose 115 billion dollars in value today while your iPhone is more popular than ever?
teardown.hook_why: It uses 'The Question' formula to create a paradox between a high-familiarity retail product (iPhone) and a massive, unexpected financial loss ($115B), forcing the viewer to stay for the explanation.

beats.said: Why did Apple lose 115 billion dollars in market cap today while your iPhone is more popular than ever?
beats.shown: A red candlestick chart of AAPL stock dropping sharply with large text: '$115B GONE'.

beats.said: The stock slipped 2.9% to $224.10, even though retail demand is holding steady.
beats.shown: A 1-day price line chart moving downward with the ticker AAPL and the percentage drop highlighted in red.

beats.said: The move wasn't about phone sales. It was a reaction to a surprise regulatory shift in the EU and rising interest rate fears.
beats.shown: Split screen: A generic 'EU Commission' building photo on one side and a 'Fed Interest Rate' arrow pointing up on the other.

beats.said: When big tech stalls, it drags your entire index fund down because Apple makes up nearly 7% of the S&P 500.
beats.shown: An S&P 500 heatmap showing Apple as a large red block compared to other tech giants.

beats.said: Not financial advice. Follow for the real reason your stocks moved today.
beats.shown: Channel logo 'Why Stocks Moved' with a 'Follow' button animation.

teardown.pacing: High-velocity cuts every 3-5 seconds. The hook lands in under 1.5 seconds with an immediate visual data point (the chart) to anchor the claim.
teardown.visual_technique: Data-heavy overlay style. Every beat features a new chart or a specific financial metric on-screen so the video remains understandable on mute.
reusable_moves: The Brand Paradox: Contrast a consumer's positive experience with a company (buying the product) against a negative market move (the stock price drop).
The Hidden Weight: Explain how one specific company's move affects the viewer's broader portfolio (e.g., its weight in the S&P 500).
teardown.remake_plan: Model 'The Question' structure by identifying a major tech stock move from today's data and framing it as a conflict between product popularity and investor sentiment.
